A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Symbolic-MoE with the same authors and core framework. All 22 pages of each version, including appendices, are readable. Text extraction and visual inspection support matching equations, tables, figures, and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracies, runtime measurements, recruitment and aggregator ablations, and appendix measurements of model performance and expert distributions.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds transfer evaluations, component sensitivity tests, trimming measurements, and token-cost analysis.

M1.justification: Both versions retain skill profiles, local/global recruitment scoring, probabilistic expert selection, 5% trimming, task-specific aggregator selection, and batched inference. Algorithm 1 and the prompts are unchanged. The new experiments test variants of existing components without revising the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 retains the original four benchmarks and adds MATH-Hard and OmniMATH (Table 5). Crucially, it evaluates transfer using AIME profiles without constructing profiles from target-benchmark validation data, substantially extending coverage to a new deployment scenario within mathematical reasoning.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators. v3 adds majority voting over recruited experts as an explicit alternative to model-based aggregation in Table 7. Reusing Debate, MoA, Self-MoA, and ReConcile on the new math benchmarks does not itself introduce new comparison methods.

E3.justification: v3 adds AIME-profile transfer protocols, keyword-model substitutions, joint expert/aggregator controls, trimming comparisons using four GPUs, and average token-count evaluation. It also marks Qwen instead of Exaone as the selected MedMCQA aggregator (v1 Table 9 versus v3 Table 11). The PDFs do not establish whether the unchanged main results were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v3 tests profile transfer (Table 5), interactions between expert and aggregator selection (Table 7), keyword-LLM sensitivity (Table 8), and trimming's accuracy/runtime effects (Table 12). Figure 5 adds token-versus-accuracy analysis. These substantially broaden examination of robustness and component behavior.

E5.justification: Both versions state that non-proprietary results are averaged over three random seeds and retain identical uncertainty entries in Table 1. New analysis tables report point estimates, consistent with earlier ablation tables; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test, or run-count policy is introduced.

E6.justification: Main Table 1 and retained ablation scores are unchanged. New results include 91.62 on MATH-Hard and 52.03 on OmniMATH, versus Self-MoA's 88.75 and 48.75, plus sensitivity, trimming, aggregation, and token-cost findings. Matched MedMCQA aggregator-validation scores change from 56.35 to 52.58 for Exaone and 56.15 to 48.02 for Granite.

T1.justification: The skill-score, recruitment, and aggregation mathematics are retained, as is the sparse-MoE formalization moved from Appendix H to Appendix M. No substantive mathematical definition, assumption, proof, or derivation is introduced or revised.

C1.justification: v3's abstract and introduction explicitly add generalization to unseen tasks, supported by transferring AIME profiles to other benchmarks. The central claims about adaptive skill routing, gradient-free model combination, the 8.15-point average advantage over the best multi-agent baseline, and efficient single-GPU execution remain.

C2.justification: v3 explains higher token use through verbose R1 experts despite lower runtime, and argues that a strong aggregator cannot compensate for weak expert selection. It also interprets trimming's GPQA benefit through retaining strong R1 experts. The original limitations concerning validation-derived profiles and keyword-model competence remain.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly identifies GPQA Diamond and documents the alternative keyword models and four-GPU trimming evaluation. Existing hardware specifications, temperatures, output limits, checkpoint identifiers, prompts, and project access information are retained; moving implementation details into Appendix C is not an additional disclosure.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for MATH, OmniMATH, Llama 3.1, and Gemma 2, while dropping WizardMath and several serving/sparse-MoA references. Related Work reattributes Self-MoA to Li et al. (2025). The principal positioning against conventional MoE and fixed-agent discussion methods remains.

P1.justification: v3 substantially condenses and rewrites the introduction, removes the lengthy methodology roadmap, separates efficiency analysis from other analyses, and moves baseline descriptions and implementation details into appendices. Appendix organization and headings are extensively revised, beyond changes required merely to insert new experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adds four tables and the two-panel token/accuracy Figure 5. Figure 3 moves from the main text to Appendix A; existing tables and figures are repositioned, several tables gain row shading, and title, heading, and document typography change substantially. The original figures are largely retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens an already substantial empirical study with profile-transfer evidence, targeted component checks, and clearer token-versus-runtime tradeoffs. These benefits are tempered by unresolved reporting issues: the selected MedMCQA aggregator changes while Table 1 remains identical, and Table 12 claims accuracy improvement despite a small MMLU-Pro decline. Overall, the additional evidence provides a modest net quality improvement.
